c05_s02 — SHARP QUBIT AXIAL FLOOR TRANSFER TO HETEROGENEOUS SPIN SITES
7 October 2026 UTC / 8 October Brisbane. Old files and INITIAL preserved.
This is a fresh transfer of an imported internally audited qubit theorem.
External specialist validation and historical priority remain UNKNOWN.

1. PRECISE IMPORTED PREMISE

For every number L>=1 of spin-1/2 sites, finite alpha_q>=0, finite real h,
and finite real delta_q<=2log2, the WHOLE L-qubit Gibbs state

 exp[(alpha_q J_q^2-delta_q J_q,z^2)/L+hJ_q,z]/Z_q

is FULLY SEPARABLE. For 0<=delta_q<=2log2 this is the internally closed
computer-assisted result of c07_s02 and independent c05_s03 verification.
For negative delta_q it follows by a real Gaussian common local filter
of the delta_q=0 state. The live accepted receipt is
 work/cycle6/c07_s02/phase2/OPTIMAL_AUDIT_CLOSED.json.
The joined proof is
 work/cycle6/c07_s02/phase2/OPTIMAL_JOIN.txt.
Its historical freeze mentions pending finite audit; the separate closure
receipt records completion. This author did not replay the 287 MB prefix
or claim a new audit of its signs. The transfer below is independently proved.

2. THE PHYSICAL SPIN COROLLARY

Let N>=1 physical sites carry arbitrary finite spins j_i=p_i/2>=0, with
integer p_i>=0 and local dimension d_i=p_i+1. Put

 M=sum_i p_i=2sum_i j_i, J=sum_i S^(i).

If M>0, finite alpha>=0 and finite h, then the physical WHOLE Gibbs state

 rho_phys proportional to exp[(alpha J^2-delta J_z^2)/N+hJ_z]

is FULLY SEPARABLE across the N physical sites whenever

 delta <= 2N log2/M = N log2/(sum_i j_i).                (V1)

Negative delta is included. If every j_i=0, the physical Hilbert space
is one-dimensional and the conclusion is trivial; no division by M is
taken. N=1 is a single site and is separable for all finite parameters,
so the displayed sufficient condition is unnecessary in that case.

For identical j>0, the sufficient range is

 delta <= log2/j.                                      (V2)

No balance condition among the spins is required. Uniform collective
coupling and a common axial field are required. This statement does not
assert optimality for j>1/2, nonuniform pair couplings, nonaxial quadratic
tensors, nonuniform fields inside the Gibbs exponent, or negative alpha.
For j=1/2 it recovers the input qubit universal floor. The higher-spin
best universal threshold remains UNKNOWN.

c05_s02 — HETEROGENEOUS-SPIN POSTERIOR PROJECTION COMPILER
7 October 2026 UTC / 8 October Brisbane. New artifact; old files preserved.
Root proposed the count/norm/posterior mechanism. This worker independently
derives its exact identities, finite-bit cost and approximation interface.
An owned bounded exact fixture accompanies this proof. Internal result;
external validation and historical priority remain UNKNOWN.

1. INPUT, OUTPUT AND THE PRE-ROUNDING INTERFACE

Let N>=1 physical blocks have integer sizes m_i=2j_i>=0 and dimensions
d_i=m_i+1. M=sum_i m_i; spin-zero blocks may be skipped after one scan.
Let U_i identify the normalized m_i-qubit symmetric Dicke basis with the
physical spin-j_i basis. U=tensor_i U_i and P=UU^dagger. M=0 is trivial.

The compiler input is a FINITE, ACQUIRED, positive structured virtual state

 Gamma=sum_(lambda=1)^K w_lambda T_(k_lambda,u_lambda,x_lambda,phi_lambda), (D1)

where weights are exact nonnegative rationals summing to one, x is rational
in[0,1], k,u>=0 with k+u<=M, and T is the UNIFORM mixture over assignments
of exactly k copies of the same normalized pure qubit

 psi(x,phi)=sqrt(1-x)|0>+sqrt(x)e^(i phi)|1>,

u computational |1> factors and M-k-u computational |0> factors. Its
assignment count is H_(M,k,u)=C(M,k)C(M-k,u). The phases have exact unit-
modulus descriptors with charged polynomial-time precision acquisition;
the intended front end uses roots of unity of order at most M+1. K and all
input descriptor lengths are charged. Uniform assignments are part of D1,
not an arbitrary permutation-invariant separable-state recognition promise.

The output is a compact finite classical sampling program. It samples an
outer label, local block counts and exactly positive rational trace-one
physical local density matrices; their tensor product is one output sample.
The expected physical state approximates normalized U^dagger Gamma U.
Its expanded mixture may have exponentially many count profiles. We claim
polynomial-size DATA and polynomial bit work per sample, not polynomially
many expanded physical product terms, a dense global matrix or hardware cost.
The projected local physical pure states are generally NOT spin-coherent.
They are arbitrary vectors in the spin-j_i site space. Site separability
does not imply all-virtual-qubit separability after projection; SU(2) rotations
alone need not prepare these vectors. Hardwar

c05_s02 — SEPARATE ALL-SIGNED PHYSICAL SPIN COMPILER COMPOSITION
7 October 2026 UTC / 8 October Brisbane. The earlier core proof, its pending
front-end paragraph and every old artifact remain preserved. This receipt
closes that composition premise using newly frozen, explicitly named sources.
Internal mathematical algorithm; not an end-to-end software/hardware benchmark.
External validation and historical priority remain UNKNOWN.

1. PRECISE FINAL MATHEMATICAL INTERFACE

Input: an explicit list m_i=2j_i of nonnegative integers at N physical sites,
M=sum_i m_i, finite BINARY RATIONAL alpha>=0, delta,h and rational requested
0<epsilon<=1. All encoded lengths are charged, including the error input.
For M>0 the input is promised to satisfy

                 delta <= 2N log2/M.                     (C1)

There is no lower bound on delta; its negative numerical magnitude and |h|
may be enormous while their binary encodings are finite. The public literal
endpoint delta=(2N/M)log2 may alternatively be supplied with the charged
constant acquisition in Section7. Arbitrary unencoded real parameters are
not admitted. M=0 has a one-dimensional output and needs no division by M.

The target is the WHOLE physical Gibbs state

 rho_phys=exp[(alpha J^2-delta J_z^2)/N+hJ_z]/Z_phys,
 J=sum_i S^(i), S_z|j_i-l>= (j_i-l)|j_i-l>.

The composed algorithm outputs polynomial-size classical data and a bounded
fair-bit sampler for arbitrary exact rational PSD trace-one local matrices
in C^(m_i+1). Each sample is their tensor-product descriptor. The expected
state has trace distance <epsilon from rho_phys. Bit computation, stored data,
precision and per-sample output/work are polynomial in numerical M, N, total
input bit lengths and log(1/epsilon). For fixed nonzero spins M=O(N).
The expanded product mixture need not have polynomially many terms.

The exact target itself is fully separable by AXIAL_SPIN_TRANSFER.txt and the
imported sharp qubit theorem. For identical j>0, C1 is delta<=log2/j; with
H=-gJ^2/N+uJ_z^2/N-h_phys J_z, g>=0, it gives the sufficient floor
T>=j u/log2 when u>=0. Negative u is admitted at every T>0. No higher-spin
optimality, exact physical iid representation or spin-coherent-only output
is claimed. N=1 (or at most one nontrivial local spin) is trivially separable
even outside C1; this composed sufficient-domain theorem does not restrict
that elementary fact.
